solutions.latex:
Asymptotes at $x=2$, $y=1$. Hence $h=-2$ and $k=1$

$\therefore y=\dfrac{a}{x-2}+1$

Sub. $\left(\dfrac{5}{2},7\right)$ to find $a$.

$7=\dfrac{a}{\frac{5}{2}-2}+1$

$6=2a$

$a=3$

$y=\dfrac{3}{x-2}+1$

$h=-2<k=1<a=3$, so $h<k<a$

$\therefore A$

$x\ne 1$, Vertical asymptote at $x=1$.

As $x\to\infty$, $\dfrac{3}{x+1}\to 0$, so horizontal asymptote at $y=2$.

solutions.latex:
$T_n=a+(n-1)d$

$a+2d,\ a+6d,\ a+15d$ are first 3 terms of GP with common ratio $r$.

$\dfrac{a+6d}{a+2d}=\dfrac{a+15d}{a+6d}$

$(a+6d)(a+6d)=(a+2d)(a+15d)$

$a^2+6ad+6ad+36d^2=a^2+15ad+2ad+30d^2$

$a^2+12ad+36d^2=a^2+17ad+30d^2$

$6d^2=5ad$

$6d=5a$ as req'd.

solutions.latex:
Horizontal transformations

Right 4 units

$f(x)=(x+1-4)^2=(x-3)^2$

Dilation factor $\dfrac{4}{3}$

$f(x)=\left(\dfrac{x}{\frac{4}{3}}-3\right)^2=\left(\dfrac{3x}{4}-3\right)^2$

Vertical transformations

Dilation factor $\dfrac{1}{3}$

$f(x)=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{3x}{4}-3\right)^2$

Down 3 units

$f(x)=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{3x}{4}-3\right)^2-3$

Reflection in $x$-axis

$f(x)=-\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{3x}{4}-3\right)^2-3\right)$

$=-\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{3x}{4}-3\right)^2+3$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: correct horizontal transformations; 1: correct final equation

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{163_q10_s1}

$f(x)=-\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{3x}{4}-3\right)^2+3$

$=-\dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}(x-4)\right)^2+3$

$=-\dfrac{1}{3}\times\dfrac{9}{16}(x-4)^2+3$

$=-\dfrac{3}{16}(x-4)^2+3$

When $y=0$, $0=-\dfrac{3}{16}(x-4)^2+3$

$-3=-\dfrac{3}{16}(x-4)^2$

$16=(x-4)^2$

$x-4=\pm 4$

$x=0$ or $x=8$

So, $y=-\dfrac{3}{16}(x-4)^2+3$ is a concave down parabola with vertex at $(4,3)$ and $x$-int. at $0$ and $8$.

notes: Cover: ABBOTSLEIGH, '2024 Higher School Certificate Assessment Task 1', Mathematics Advanced, total 65 marks (Section I 5 marks Q1-5, Section II 60 marks Q6-10, 12 marks each); matches expected label 2024 Abbotsleigh AT1 (2024 HSC cohort). No sitting date is printed, so whether it was sat in Term 4 2023 or early 2024 cannot be told; graduation year 2024 either way. PDF is 76 pages: pages 0-37 the blank booklet, pages 38-75 the same booklet with handwritten teacher solutions (green) and red mark allocations. Questions transcribed from pages 2-34; solutions from 40-72. Skipped: page 1 outcomes, blank pages, extra writing pages. Blank answer axes/grids in Q8(b)(i), Q9(b)(iii), Q9(c), Q10(c)(ii) are answer space and were not cropped. Q8(b) has no shared text (the paper goes straight to (b)(i)), so its container part has empty latex. Q10 page 35 header reads '(c) (continued)' in the question copy but '(b) (continued)' in the solution copy. Solution sketches are cropped from the solution copy with the red marking annotations whitened out. MCQ answers are circled with handwritten working on the paper (source extracted); Q3 working runs off the page bottom, the final comparison line was completed. Source slips transcribed as written: Q7(c)(ii) working writes f(x) for g(x); Q9(b)(i) second line -3x/(4+x^2) drops the square; Q9(b)(ii) first line drops the minus sign (3x^2/x^2); Q9(c) writes 3/(x+1) -> 0 and 'y-intercept at -1/2' (should be -1; the sketch shows (0,-1)). Unrelated parts are grouped under Questions 6-10 as printed (split_questions.py can split them after loading). No old-syllabus or Standard-course content.
